passage:
“Jasleen, give Nani a kiss goodnight,” said Rajni. Jasleen leaned over, lips pushed into a small round pucker, and pressed them against the phone screen.
“Mmmwah!” said Nani from the phone.
“Now shoes,” said Rajni. Jasleen sat down and sucked her lips in, tongue out a little, pulling at a strap.
“You're working hard.”
Then the doorbell rang and Jasleen stretched her lips wide and squealed, “Papa!”

qa.q: What did Jasleen press her puckered lips against?
qa.a: The phone screen, to kiss Nani goodnight.

qa.q: What might Jasleen's stretched lips and squeal at the doorbell mean, and what alternative is there?
qa.a: They most likely show excitement that Papa is home. They might also just be a loud reaction to the doorbell sound.

qa.q: What could Rajni do to build on this play?
qa.a: Rajni could name each feeling as it happens, like “You're excited!”, and copy the kiss or the squeal back playfully.

qa.q: How might Nani feel receiving a kiss through the phone?
qa.a: She probably feels loved and delighted that her granddaughter did it on her own, even from far away.

grounding: A toddler puckers for a kiss, sucks in her lips in concentration and stretches them in an excited squeal.

passage: Playgroup note, Wednesday. Pallavi, two, puckered her lips and gave her doll a loud kiss during the tea-party game. Later, threading big wooden beads, she pulled her lips tightly in and held them there until the bead went on. When rain began on the roof, she stretched her mouth wide and squealed with her arms flapping. Same little mouth, three different meanings. I will keep watching what she is doing each time before guessing. 🙂 Himani

qa.q: What was Pallavi doing when she sucked her lips in?
qa.a: She was threading big wooden beads.

qa.q: What did Pallavi's wide mouth and squeal at the rain show she was feeling?
qa.a: It probably shows excitement, since her arms flapped as well. It could also be a reaction to the sudden sound of rain on the roof.

qa.q: What is Himani's plan for reading Pallavi's mouth shapes?
qa.a: Himani will look at what Pallavi is doing each time before guessing, because the same lip movement can mean different things.

qa.q: How might Pallavi's mother feel hearing this?
qa.a: She may enjoy hearing her daughter is exploring so many ways to show feelings, and may notice them herself at home.

grounding: A toddler puckers, tightens and stretches her lips in different contexts, each with a different meaning.

passage:
In the courtyard of their small-town house, Anirban's uncle Nitin sat with him on the mat. Anirban was trying to push a wooden ring onto a stick. He sucked both lips in until they almost vanished, his eyes fixed on the ring. It slid on. He let his lips out with a pop.
When the bus horn sounded and Nitin stood to leave, Anirban puckered up his lips and pushed his face forward for a kiss.

qa.q: What was Anirban trying to push onto the stick?
qa.a: A wooden ring.

qa.q: What do Anirban's two lip movements suggest about his feelings?
qa.a: Sucking his lips in suggests concentration while working on the ring; puckering for a kiss at the end suggests fondness for Nitin, and maybe some sadness that he was leaving.

qa.q: How could Nitin respond to the puckered lips?
qa.a: He could bend down, accept the kiss and say a warm goodbye, so Anirban's affection is met.

qa.q: How might Nitin feel when Anirban offers the kiss?
qa.a: He would probably feel touched and a little reluctant to catch the bus.

grounding: A toddler sucks in his lips while concentrating and puckers them for a goodbye kiss, the meaning changing with the moment.

passage:
The water jets in the Singapore park shot up without warning. Mei stretched her lips wide and let out a high squeal, arms flapping. Amara, her nanny, froze for a second. Was that a scream?
Mei ran straight back into the spray, squealing again, lips stretched in a grin, and looked back to see if Amara was watching.
Amara relaxed and clapped. "Again? Go on!"

qa.q: What made Mei squeal?
qa.a: The water jets in the park shooting up without warning.

qa.q: What was Amara worried about when Mei first squealed?
qa.a: She was worried it might be a scream of fear; when Mei ran back into the spray grinning, it was clear the squeal was excitement.

qa.q: What helped Amara tell excitement from fear here?
qa.a: Watching what Mei did next, running back and looking round to share it, instead of judging the squeal alone.

qa.q: How does Mei seem to experience the water jets?
qa.a: She seems thrilled and eager to share her joy, looking back to check Amara was watching.

grounding: A toddler stretches her lips in a squeal of excitement that a nanny first mistakes for fear, until the context shows joy.

passage: I'm Yogesh, and I live across the landing from little Himani. When I open my door, she's often at her grille. Yesterday she saw me, pushed her lips out in a tight pucker and pressed her face to the bars. I didn't know if it was a kiss or the fish face her sister taught her. I puckered back. She made a smacking sound, then stretched her lips wide and squealed. Her mother waved. I think it was a kiss.

qa.q: Where does Himani often stand when Yogesh opens the door?
qa.a: At her grille.

qa.q: What might Himani's pucker have meant?
qa.a: It might have been a friendly kiss, showing fondness for Yogesh, or the fish face her sister taught her; her smacking sound and excited squeal suggest she was happy to see Yogesh.

qa.q: What did Yogesh do that was a good response?
qa.a: Yogesh puckered back gently, joining the game without deciding for sure what it meant.

qa.q: How might Himani's mother see the exchange?
qa.a: She probably finds it sweet and friendly, which is why she waves.

grounding: A neighbour sees a toddler pucker and then stretch her lips in a squeal, unsure if it is a kiss or play.

passage:
Tuesday night: “Goodnight kiss?” asked her father, Dhruv. Tanuja puckered her lips into a tiny circle and pressed them to his cheek.
Thursday morning: she sat with the shape sorter, lips sucked right in, pushing the star at the square hole, then the star hole.
Saturday evening: Dhruv came home from a work trip. Tanuja saw him at the door, stretched her lips wide and let out a long squeal, bouncing on the spot.

qa.q: What was Tanuja pushing at the shape sorter?
qa.a: She was pushing the star at the square hole, then the star hole.

qa.q: What does Tanuja's wide-stretched mouth and squeal suggest she felt on Saturday?
qa.a: It suggests she was excited and thrilled to see her father back; the same lips meant affection on Tuesday and concentration on Thursday.

qa.q: How can a parent read a toddler's lip movements well?
qa.a: By looking at the context each time, such as a kiss, a puzzle or a homecoming, instead of giving one meaning to one movement.

qa.q: What is it like for Dhruv to get that squeal at the door?
qa.a: He likely feels welcomed and loved, knowing she missed him during the trip.

grounding: It shows a toddler puckering for a kiss, sucking her lips in while concentrating and stretching them in an excited squeal, meanings shifting with context.
